high.title: Koo Yun-chul: 'FX Rate to Stabilize Once External Factors Like Foreign Rebalancing Subside'
high.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy Koo Yun-chul signaled confidence in KRW stabilization during a National Assembly Finance and Economic Planning Committee session, stating that the exchange rate will normalize "once external factors subside, considering economic fundamentals and soundness." His remarks came in direct response to a parliamentary question on exchange rate stabilization measures, suggesting the government is actively monitoring FX volatility but is not yet signaling imminent direct intervention. The reference to "foreign rebalancing" as the key external driver is significant — this points to global portfolio rebalancing flows (likely USD strength and EM outflows) as the primary force pressuring KRW rather than domestic fundamentals. For KRW traders, this is a moderately dovish signal from the government: policymakers believe current weakness is transitory and externally driven, which reduces the probability of aggressive FX intervention in the near term. Bond investors should note that if KRW stabilizes organically, BOK may have more room to maintain or ease its policy rate stance without imported inflation concerns. **Watch for:** any follow-up BOK commentary on the FX pass-through to inflation, and whether USD/KRW tests key resistance levels near 1,380–1,400.

---

high.title: USD-KRW Plunges to Early 1,510s on Korea-Japan Coordination News, Suspected Intervention
high.summary:
The USD-KRW exchange rate fell sharply to the early 1,510s during London trading hours on July 7th, with the pair trading at 1,513.10 won as of 8:26 PM Seoul time — a decline of 17.20 won from the prior day's 3:30 PM close of 1,530.30 won. The move represents a 16.90 won drop from the 6:00 AM New York close. The pair opened the session at approximately 1,528.90 won before reversing sharply lower. The catalyst appears to be news of Korea-Japan currency coordination, alongside suspected official intervention by Korean authorities. This is a highly significant development for KRW traders: a confirmed coordination signal between Seoul and Tokyo suggests both governments are actively pushing back against USD strength, potentially marking a medium-term inflection point for the won. Traders should monitor whether the BOK sustains intervention pressure and whether USD-KRW breaks and holds below 1,510. Any official statement from the BOK or Ministry of Finance confirming the coordination would add further downside momentum to the pair. Watch the 1,500 psychological level as the next key support zone.

---

high.title: KOSPI Plunges 4.91% After Intraday 8% Drop Triggers Circuit Breaker
high.summary: South Korea's KOSPI index suffered a severe sell-off, closing down 4.91% at 7,656.31 — a drop of 395.02 points — marking the sixth circuit breaker trigger of the year, with four occurring since June alone. The intraday decline exceeded 8% before the trading halt, after which losses partially recovered. This scale of equity market dislocation carries significant implications across asset classes. For KRW, a KOSPI rout of this magnitude typically accelerates foreign equity outflows, putting sharp depreciation pressure on the won as foreign investors repatriate capital. For Korean government bonds (KTBs), a flight-to-safety dynamic could temporarily support demand, compressing short-end yields, though broader risk-off sentiment may also dampen foreign appetite for EM fixed income. The frequency of circuit breakers in 2026 — four in less than six weeks — signals deteriorating market confidence and elevated volatility. Fund managers should closely monitor foreign net equity selling data, USD/KRW spot levels for intervention signals from the Bank of Korea, and any emergency policy response from financial authorities. This is a critical risk event requiring immediate portfolio reassessment.

high.title: Korean Stocks Battered for 3rd Consecutive Day by Middle East Risk and AI Chip Peak-Out Fears
high.summary: South Korea's equity market extended its losing streak into a third consecutive session, with the KOSPI closing down 4.91% at 7,656.31 on July 7, as investors dismissed Samsung Electronics' record-high preliminary Q2 2026 earnings guidance. The dual headwinds of escalating Middle East geopolitical risk and growing fears over a peak-out in AI chip demand are driving broad risk aversion toward Korean equities, which are heavily weighted toward semiconductor and technology exporters. For KRW/USD traders, this sustained sell-off amplifies depreciation risks as foreign investors reduce Korean equity exposure — historically one of the most reliable drivers of won weakness. Samsung's strong earnings failing to provide any market support is a bearish signal suggesting macro and geopolitical concerns are overwhelming fundamentals. The persistence of the sell-off also raises the probability of Bank of Korea FX intervention or verbal guidance to stabilize the won. Watch for BOK reserve drawdown data, any policy statements, and whether foreign selling in the equity market is mirrored by bond outflows, which would compound KRW downside pressure significantly.

high.title: IMF Raises South Korea's Growth Forecast to 2.6% from 1.9% — Highest Among G20 Advanced Economies
high.summary:
The IMF has sharply upgraded South Korea's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 2.6%, up from 1.9% previously — the strongest upward revision among G20 advanced economies and placing Korea at the top of that peer group. The 2027 forecast was also lifted to 2.5%, a 0.4 percentage point increase. The revision is driven primarily by resilient semiconductor export performance, which the IMF judges to be more than sufficient to offset headwinds from the ongoing Middle East conflict. In contrast, global growth was trimmed 0.1pp to 3.0%, the US was left unchanged, Japan was cut 0.1pp, and China was nudged up 0.2pp. For KRW traders, this is a meaningfully bullish signal: a relative growth upgrade of this magnitude — while the broader global outlook softens — supports KRW on a fundamental basis and reduces the near-term probability of emergency BOK easing. Bond investors should note that stronger growth combined with the inflation revision flagged in the ADB article (see below) could shift the yield curve modestly steeper. Watch for BOK's reaction at its next rate decision and any FX positioning shifts from offshore players re-rating Korean macro.

---

high.title: Dollar-Won Breaches 1,510 on Trump's Threat of 'Another Iran Strike Today'
high.summary:
The dollar-won exchange rate broke above 1,510 won during overnight New York trading, reaching 1,512.10 won as of 1:15 a.m. KST on July 9th. This represents a significant move lower for KRW, driven by a sharp risk-off episode following Trump's threat of another military strike against Iran. Surging international oil prices amplified the risk-off sentiment, reinforcing dollar strength and pressuring the won. Notably, despite the intraday breach of 1,510, the rate was still trading materially below the previous Seoul session close of 1,528.30 won — a decline of 16.20 won — suggesting some overnight stabilization or position unwinding.

**Key implications for KRW traders:** The 1,510 level has served as a psychologically significant threshold. A sustained breach raises the risk of accelerated won weakness, particularly if oil prices remain elevated (Korea is a major net oil importer, which worsens the current account at the margin). Traders should monitor whether the BOK intervenes via state-bank dollar selling, and whether the Seoul open on July 9th confirms the overnight directional shift. U.S.-Iran escalation risk remains the dominant near-term driver — watch for any further geopolitical developments overnight.

high.title: US 10-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand — Yield Below Expectations
high.summary:
The U.S. Treasury's $39 billion 10-year note reopening auction on July 8th (local time) cleared at a yield of 4.580%, coming in 4.2 basis points below pre-auction market expectations — a strong "stop-through" signal indicating robust demand. Critically, the indirect bidder rate (a proxy for foreign/overseas demand) hit its highest level since September last year, suggesting sustained international appetite for U.S. Treasuries despite elevated geopolitical uncertainty.

**Implications for KRW and Korean bonds:** A well-bid U.S. 10-year auction with strong foreign demand has mixed read-throughs for Korean markets. On one hand, anchored or slightly declining U.S. yields reduce the rate differential pressure on Korean government bonds (KTBs) and could ease some capital outflow concerns. On the other hand, robust foreign demand for USTs may reflect a flight-to-quality dynamic that simultaneously draws capital away from emerging market assets including KRW and KTBs. The 4.58% clearing yield remains historically elevated and continues to present a competitive yield alternative to KTBs. Bond managers should track the 10yr UST/KTB spread for signs of relative value shifts and any corresponding moves in foreign KTB holdings.

medium.title: Homeplus Bankruptcy Crisis Rattles Financial Sector as FSS Summons Lenders
medium.summary:
The Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) has launched a rapid-fire series of consultations with financial institutions — banks on July 7th, insurers on July 8th, and non-bank lenders on July 9th — to assess exposure to Homeplus leased store assets amid the retailer's impending bankruptcy. The FSS is scrutinizing loan portfolios and gauging the sector's capacity to absorb potential credit losses. While Homeplus is a retail entity, this event carries **systemic relevance** for the Korean banking sector: concentrated credit exposure to a large distressed borrower could tighten domestic credit conditions, weigh on bank profitability, and — if losses prove material — modestly pressure KRW through risk-off sentiment among foreign investors monitoring Korean financial stability. The FSS's proactive intervention signals regulatory concern about contagion risk. Bond investors should watch whether any major lender discloses material provisions, which could widen Korean bank credit spreads. FX traders should monitor whether foreign portfolio investors reduce Korean financial sector exposure in response, which could add incremental selling pressure on KRW. The breadth and sequencing of FSS consultations suggest the situation is still being assessed rather than contained.

---

medium.title: GDP Now Raises Q2 U.S. Growth Forecast to 1.4%, Up 0.2 Percentage Points — Import-Driven Drag Narrows
medium.summary: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model revised its Q2 2025 U.S. annualized growth estimate upward to 1.4% from 1.2%, with the improvement driven by a narrowing of the import drag on GDP. While still modest relative to the model's initial April reading of 3.7%, the upward revision suggests U.S. economic resilience is stabilizing at a low but positive level. For KRW and Korean bond traders, a firmer U.S. growth print reduces the urgency of Fed rate cuts, supporting USD strength and maintaining headwinds for KRW in the near term. However, a narrowing import drag may also indicate softening U.S. domestic demand, which could weigh on Korean export orders and the trade balance outlook — a secondary negative for KRW. **Watch for:** upcoming U.S. CPI and NFP data, which will be the critical determinants of Fed policy trajectory and USD/KRW direction.

medium.title: National Assembly Finance Committee Holds First Plenary Session — Ruling Party Appoints Oh Ki-hyung as Floor Leader, PPP Boycotts
medium.summary: The National Assembly's Finance and Economy Planning Committee convened its first plenary session for the second half of the 22nd National Assembly, appointing Democratic Party lawmaker Oh Ki-hyung as floor leader amid a boycott by the opposition People Power Party (PPP). The committee also received business reports from related government agencies. For market participants, the composition and political dynamics of the Finance Committee matter for fiscal and financial regulatory legislation — a PPP boycott signals continued political gridlock, which may delay passage of any fiscal stimulus or financial reform bills. While not an immediate market mover, persistent legislative paralysis is a mild negative for investor sentiment toward Korean equities and could delay any supplementary budget measures that might support growth. **Watch for:** whether the political standoff affects the timeline for any planned fiscal spending or financial sector reform legislation.

medium.title: Strong Demand at US 3-Year Treasury Auction Pushes Yields Below Expectations
medium.summary: The US Treasury auctioned $58 billion in 3-year notes at a yield of 4.179%, 1.3 basis points below the prior month's 4.192%, with the Primary Dealer takedown hitting its lowest level since 2004 — a sign of strong end-user demand. Robust demand at the short end of the US curve suggests investors remain comfortable anchoring near-term rate expectations, which could cap upward pressure on US yields in the near term. For Korean bond investors, a stable or declining US short-end yield environment reduces the rate differential pressure on KTBs and supports the BOK's capacity to maintain or ease its policy stance. This is a constructive backdrop for Korean government bonds, particularly shorter-duration instruments.

medium.title: US Treasuries Fall on Reports of Vessel Attack in Strait of Hormuz
medium.summary: US Treasury prices edged lower after reports emerged that Iran attacked a merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing oil prices higher and weighing on bond prices. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.497%, up 1.70 basis points. Rising oil prices driven by geopolitical risk in the Strait of Hormuz carry direct implications for Korea, a major energy importer — higher crude costs would widen Korea's import bill, pressure the trade balance, and add inflationary headwinds that could complicate the BOK's easing path. KRW may face renewed depreciation pressure if the Hormuz situation escalates, partially offsetting today's sharp won appreciation. Bond traders should watch whether the 10-year UST yield sustains above 4.50%, as this would increase pressure on KTB yields and the KRW simultaneously.

medium.title: France's Le Pen Cleared to Run for President as Bond Yields Surge
medium.summary: French government bond yields extended gains after Marine Le Pen received a reduced sentence on appeal, effectively clearing her path to contest next year's French presidential election. The development drove a repricing of French sovereign risk, pushing OAT yields higher. While this is primarily a European story, the risk-off spillover from rising European sovereign spreads can affect global EM sentiment and appetite for Korean assets. A broader selloff in European bonds could push global yields higher, creating headwinds for KTBs. International fund managers with cross-market exposure should monitor French political developments as a potential source of global duration risk through the remainder of 2025.

medium.title: Shinhan Investment Corp. Secures 1.5 Trillion Won in Corporate Bond Demand
medium.summary:
Shinhan Investment Corp. attracted 1.595 trillion won (~$1.35 billion) in bookbuilding demand against a 250 billion won corporate bond issuance — a roughly 6.4x oversubscription ratio. The 2-year tranche alone drew 885 billion won in orders against a 150 billion won target. Despite the severe equity market turmoil on the same day, this exceptionally strong corporate bond demand suggests domestic institutional investors are rotating out of equities and into fixed-income instruments, consistent with a flight-to-safety dynamic within Korean credit markets. For KTB traders, robust demand for high-grade corporate paper from a major financial institution implies the short-to-medium end of the Korean rates curve retains domestic support even amid broader market stress. This is worth monitoring as a leading indicator of broader fixed-income demand trends.

---

medium.title: ADB Raises South Korea's 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.6%, Up 0.7pp — Inflation Revised Up to 2.7% from 2.3%
medium.summary:
The Asian Development Bank has revised South Korea's 2026 growth forecast upward by 0.7 percentage points to 2.6%, citing a cushioning effect from Middle East-related policy response measures. The 2027 growth projection was also raised modestly to 2.0% (+0.1pp). Critically for fixed income and FX markets, the ADB simultaneously revised its 2026 inflation forecast higher to 2.7% from 2.3% — a 40bp upward adjustment that, combined with the stronger growth outlook, materially complicates the BOK's room to cut rates further. For KRW bond traders, the inflation upgrade is the more actionable data point: if the BOK perceives inflation risks as re-emerging alongside resilient growth, front-end KTB yields could face upward pressure and rate cut expectations may need to be pared back. KRW bulls will view the dual growth upgrades from both the IMF and ADB in the same week as reinforcing support for the currency.

---

medium.title: French Bond Yields Surge for Consecutive Days as 'Le Pen Pricing' Takes Hold
medium.summary:
French 10-year government bond yields are rising for a second consecutive session as bond markets begin pricing in the political risk associated with Marine Le Pen's path to the presidential election and her lead in polling. This "Le Pen pricing" dynamic is contributing to broader European sovereign bond volatility and widening French-German spreads. While not directly a Korean market story, the spillover effect matters: rising European sovereign risk premiums can contribute to global risk-off sentiment, indirectly weighing on EM currencies including KRW. Additionally, any material dislocation in European bond markets could affect global duration positioning and capital allocation decisions by institutional investors with cross-market mandates. Fund managers with multi-EM exposure should monitor French OAT spreads as a secondary risk sentiment indicator alongside the more dominant U.S.-Iran geopolitical driver currently in play.

---

medium.title: KOSPI Falls for Third Straight Day to Close Below 7,200 — Retail Investors Turn Sellers
medium.summary:
The KOSPI closed at 7,246.79, down 5.35% on the day — its third consecutive session of losses — as both institutional and retail investors turned net sellers. The catalyst for the afternoon selloff was news of military conflict between the United States and Iran, which rattled risk sentiment broadly. Semiconductor heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which had been attempting to stabilize despite peak-cycle concerns, extended losses following the geopolitical headlines. For KRW traders, a sustained equity selloff of this magnitude warrants close attention: significant foreign portfolio outflows from Korean equities would exert depreciation pressure on the Won, potentially prompting BOK monitoring or verbal intervention. Watch whether foreign net selling accelerates in the coming sessions, which could widen the KRW/USD spread and lift short-end government bond yields if risk-off flows intensify.

---
